findings_qualitative.value: High-density tracers H13CO+ and C17O (J=3-2) are not detected toward MMS-1, and there is no extended high-density envelope connecting to the disk, indicating the disk is detached from the surrounding dense core.

findings_qualitative.value: High-temperature (~50 K) 12CO (J=3-2) gas is detected several hundred au away from MMS-1, indicating shock heating from turbulent gas interactions.

evidence.quote: The present $^{12}$CO ($J$ = 3–2) observations also found very high-temperature ($\sim$50 K) gas component at several hundred au away from MMS-1, indicating that there was shock heating possibly caused by interactions among the turbulent gases.

claims.hypothesis: The very low-luminosity protostar MMS-1 in MC27/L1521F hosts a compact rotating Keplerian disk around a ~0.2 M_odot central star that is detached from the surrounding dense core.
claims.experiment: Observed MMS-1 with ALMA Band 7 in 0.87 mm continuum and 12CO, H13CO+, and C17O at ~0.18'' x 0.10'' resolution, and modeled the 12CO kinematics and continuum with synthetic CASA observations of a 3D LTE Keplerian disk.
claims.result: Detected a (12.9 +- 1.4 au) x (7.8 +- 0.6 au) dust disk and high-velocity 12CO emission best fit by M_* = 0.18 +- 0.05 M_odot, R_disk = 9 AU, and M_disk = 8 x 10^-5 M_odot, with no detection of extended envelope gas in H13CO+ or C17O.
claims.finding: MMS-1 is a ~0.2 M_odot protostar surrounded by a tiny (~10 AU, ~10^-4 M_odot) Keplerian disk detached from the surrounding ~10^6 cm^-3 dense core, where mass accretion has nearly halted.

evidence.loc: Physical quantities of disk of MMS-1
evidence.quote: The derived optimum values of the Keplerian disk model are $M_{*}$ = 0.18 $M_{\odot}$, $R_{\rm disk}$ = 9 AU, $M_{\rm disk}$ = 8 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$ $M_{\odot}$ and $T_{\rm 1au}$ = 180 K.

evidence.loc: Gas/dust distributions toward MMS-1
evidence.quote: These results indicate that the disk may be detached from the surrounding environment although it is located at the center of the dense core whose density is $\sim$10$^6$ cm$^{-3}$.

evidence.loc: Conclusions
evidence.quote: The current low mass accretion rate may indicate that the mass accretion onto the protostar/disk has halted quite recently.

claims.hypothesis: The broken density profile of the MC27/L1521F core (r^-1.4 inside 3000 au, r^-2.0 outside) can be reconciled with the inside-out collapse model once the newly measured central stellar mass of ~0.2 M_odot is accounted for.
claims.experiment: Calculated the expansion wave propagation timescale to 3000 au at c_s = 0.2 km s^-1 (10 K) and the accumulated stellar mass under standard inside-out collapse accretion rates.
claims.result: The expansion wave reaches 3000 au in 7 x 10^4 years, accumulating ~0.1 M_odot at an accretion rate of 1.6 x 10^-6 M_odot yr^-1, whereas a higher rate of 1 x 10^-5 M_odot yr^-1 forms the star before the wave reaches 3000 au.
claims.finding: The inside-out collapse model can explain the observed core density profile and stellar mass if the accretion rate was ~1.6 x 10^-6 M_odot yr^-1 over ~7 x 10^4 years.

evidence.loc: A detached disk at the center of an isolated protostellar core
evidence.quote: The time scale of the expansion wave reaching the breaking radius of 3000 au becomes 7 $\times$10$^4$ years.

evidence.loc: A detached disk at the center of an isolated protostellar core
evidence.quote: If we assume the accretion rate after the protostar core formation to be 1.6 $\times$ 10$^{-6}$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ (cite: Shu77), the mass of the formed star becomes $\sim$0.1 $M_{\odot}$ within the time scale; the inside-out collapse model can explain the observed density profile in this case.

claims.hypothesis: The very low luminosity (<0.1 L_odot) of the young ~0.2 M_odot protostar can be explained by pre-main-sequence stellar evolution with cold accretion.
claims.experiment: Computed stellar luminosity evolution using the Hosokawa numerical code with cold accretion at 10^-5 M_odot yr^-1 up to 0.2 M_odot followed by halting accretion.
claims.result: Classical tracks require >1 Myr to fade below 0.1 L_odot, whereas cold accretion starting from a 0.01 M_odot seed with a very small initial radius of 0.65 R_odot reaches ~0.07 L_odot in <10^5 years after accretion halts.
claims.finding: Cold accretion can reproduce the observed low luminosity of the young 0.2 M_odot protostar, but only if an unusually small initial protostellar radius (~0.65 R_odot vs standard 4 R_odot) is assumed, whose physical origin remains unknown.

evidence.loc: Abstract
evidence.quote: However, we cannot explain the observed low luminosity with the standard pre-main-sequence evolutionary track unless we assume cold accretion with an extremely small initial radius of the protostar ($\sim$0.65 $R_\odot$).

evidence.loc: A very low-luminosity object as a candidate evolved by cold accretion
evidence.quote: Our calculation starting with a 0.01 $M_{\odot}$ star with the initial radius of 0.65 $R_{\odot}$ reproduces the observed luminosity ($\sim$0.07 $L_{\odot}$) in $<$10$^5$ years after we stop the mass accretion.

evidence.loc: A very low-luminosity object as a candidate evolved by cold accretion
evidence.quote: Mechanisms to create such small stellar core and environments that enable the cold accretion are currently unknown.

referee_caveats_inferred: The disk radius (~9 au) is smaller than the synthesized beam (25 au x 14 au), so the Keplerian rotation curve and break radius rely heavily on sub-beam centroid fitting (spectroastrometry) and forward modeling assumptions.
Only the blueshifted wing and a narrow range of redshifted channels are uncontaminated by foreground core absorption, limiting dynamical constraints on symmetry and Keplerian profile.
The disk mass estimate assumes optically thin 0.87 mm dust emission and a fixed gas-to-dust ratio of 100, which may underestimate mass if the compact 9 au disk is optically thick at Band 7.

An inconsistency exists between Section 4.1 (which argues 10^-5 M_odot yr^-1 is too fast for the expansion wave to reach 3000 au) and Section 4.2 (which adopts 10^-5 M_odot yr^-1 in the cold accretion calculation).
